statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases from 19 to 18 now that Oracle's fiscal first-quarter results have printed and beaten expectations, removing the unknown that justified the previous step up. Cash NAS100 closed at 29,103.51, down 318.04 points or 1.08%, inside a 29,038.22 to 29,250.41 band whose low was never retested after the opening hour. NQ futures paused the CME maintenance halt at 29,143.25, down 1.04%, having covered 29,044.25 to 29,508.25 overnight. VIX is 17.84 to 17.93, up about 8.4%, beneath an 18.17 high. The ten-year is near 4.91%, its highest since 2023, against 4.83% on 9 September, and the two-year is near 4.59% against 4.43%. WTI is quoted near $103.93 and Brent near $108.95 after settlements of $102.48 and $107.63.
recommendation: Tail at 18 maps the policy state to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with pause false and caution false under the fixed repository mapping. The step down from 19 reflects one specific change: the post-close earnings unknown that raised the previous reading has resolved, and it resolved constructively, with Oracle reporting revenue up 30% and remaining performance obligations of $664 billion. Offsetting that, CME equity futures are inside the 21:00 to 22:00 UTC maintenance halt, so no NQ price path is observable in this hour, and the conference call is still running. Neither condition is evidence of directional structure. The danger window stays drawn narrowly around 12:30 to 14:00 UTC on 11 September, covering the August consumer price release, the first hour of post-release discovery and the 13:30 UTC cash open. Stress at 86 remains the elevated part of this assessment and does not by itself change the mapped state.
headline: NQ futures pause the CME halt at 29,143.25, down 1.04%, after a cash session contained inside a 212-point band; tail eases 19 to 18 as Oracle's beat resolves the post-close unknown constructively, while Brent near $108.95 and a ten-year at 2023 highs keep stress at 86.
body:
The hour that closes the trading day changes the catalyst position rather than the structure. Oracle published fiscal first-quarter results at 20:10 UTC: total revenue of $19.3 billion, up 30%, total cloud revenue of $11.6 billion, up 62%, cloud infrastructure revenue of $7.4 billion, up 121%, non-GAAP earnings of $1.92 per share, and remaining performance obligations of $664 billion, an increase of $209 billion year over year. Fiscal 2027 guidance was set at a minimum of $90 billion in revenue and $8.10 in non-GAAP earnings per share. Shares were quoted roughly 7% higher after hours against a regular session that closed down 5.38%. The previous assessment raised tail from 17 to 19 specifically because a large single-stock earnings impulse was about to reprice in thin post-close liquidity with an unknown outcome. That outcome is now known and it is constructive, so the step is partly given back.

The index structure itself has not changed. Cash NAS100 closed at 29,103.51, down 318.04 points or 1.08%, and the entire session fitted inside a 212-point band between 29,038.22 and 29,250.41. The opening-auction low was set in the first hour and was never revisited. NQ futures paused at 29,143.25, down 1.04%, inside a 29,044.25 to 29,508.25 overnight range. This is the observation the framework weights most heavily, because tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach, not the size of a decline. Thursday's path repeatedly offered retracement in both directions.

It is also worth stating plainly what is not observable right now. CME equity futures are inside their daily 21:00 to 22:00 UTC maintenance halt, so there is no live NQ price path in this clock-hour, and Oracle's conference call began at 21:00 UTC with no outcome yet published. The reopening at 22:00 UTC is therefore the transmission checkpoint at which the after-hours repricing can first reach the index. Confidence is held at 85 rather than lowered further because current verified levels, yields, energy prices, volatility and the release calendar are all in hand; only this single hour of price path is missing, and it is missing by schedule.

The macro and cross-asset backdrop is what keeps stress extreme. August producer prices, published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics at 12:30 UTC, rose 0.4% month over month and 5.4% year over year, with final demand goods up 1.1% on energy. The ten-year Treasury yield climbed to about 4.91%, its highest level since 2023, from 4.83% on 9 September, and the two-year sits near 4.59% against 4.43%. Crude extended sharply, with WTI quoted near $103.93 and Brent near $108.95 after settlements of $102.48 and $107.63, the highest since May, on an unresolved Persian Gulf conflict in which Saudi output has fallen to its lowest since 1990 and Iran has said it will announce an exclusion zone near the Strait of Hormuz within days or weeks. Thursday's latest-session sector context showed semiconductors notably weaker than the broader index. The majors closed lower for a fourth consecutive session.

The forward window is shaped by one scheduled event. The August consumer price report is released at 12:30 UTC on 11 September, the last inflation reading before the FOMC decision on 16 September, with consensus near 3.3% to 3.4% headline year over year and 2.4% core. Conditional tail peaks at 23 in that slot and again at 13:00 UTC where post-release discovery overlaps the cash open. Both map to WATCH and neither reaches the block threshold of 25, because no post-release price path is observed at publication time and, under this framework, surprise magnitude and forecast dispersion raise stress and widen uncertainty before they raise tail. What would raise tail is observed: an opening auction that extends without meaningful retracement, repeated extension after failed pullbacks, or price holding near session extremes. None of that is in evidence tonight.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 21:00 UTC on 9 September to 20:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 9 and holds a tight 8 to 11 band through the U.S. overnight, the Asian session and the European morning, with the dominant mode recorded as mixed throughout. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and a 24 peak at 13:00 UTC covering post-release discovery and the cash open, the only two slots in the window that mapped to WATCH. The final seven slots record the decay back into range and then a modest rebuild: 17, 14, then 16 as yields and crude extended, 15, 16, 17 into the final cash hour and 19 at 20:00 UTC as Oracle's results landed after the close. Stress never left the extreme band, running 80 to 87 throughout, which is the defining feature of this window: a persistently difficult environment in which the observed price path nevertheless kept offering retracement.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens in the CME maintenance halt on 10 September and ends in the New York afternoon of 11 September. Conditional tail starts at 18 and holds there across the 22:00 UTC reopening, the checkpoint at which Oracle's after-hours repricing can first transmit to the index, then eases to 16 late in the evening. It decays through 14 and 12 into the Asian session and settles at an 11 floor across the quiet Asian hours, where no U.S. macro is scheduled. From the European pre-market it rebuilds gradually, 12 through 14, and reaches 15 in the final full hour before the release. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report and 23 again at 13:00 UTC where post-release discovery overlaps the 13:30 UTC cash open; both map to WATCH and neither reaches the block threshold, since no post-release price path is observed. The path then eases to 20 at the University of Michigan release, then 17, 15, 14 and 14 through the New York afternoon, before ticking to 15 and 16 in the last two hours as pre-weekend adjustment concentrates into a week that has closed lower four sessions running with an unresolved Persian Gulf conflict carrying across the weekend. Stress stays in the extreme band throughout, peaking at 90 around the release, and confidence declines steadily from 85 to 60 with distance from observed evidence.
